items.headline: SpaceX plans a Sept. 28 Starship launch with 26 V3 satellites.
items.current: Starship shifts into paid orbital missions
paragraphs: For European buyers staring at a tightening global manifest, Starlink now ties near-term network expansion to Starship: it says Starship will launch 26 V3 Starlink satellites on Sept. 28. SpaceX has also moved Booster 21 to the pad and is flying reused heat-shield tiles on Ship 41 as it tries to turn Flight 14 into the first Starship orbital insertion.

SpaceX separately says it plans to end commercial Falcon 9 launches in the next few years. That puts extra weight on whether Starship can show repeatable orbit and reentry, not just a single attempt, because any credible Starship ramp changes how far ahead non‑SpaceX capacity gets booked.

block.head: Flight 14’s run-up is now anchored to Starlink V3 deployment

points.text: SpaceX said Ship 41 will reuse heat-shield tiles from Ship 40.
SpaceX moved Booster 21 to the Starbase pad.
SpaceX positioned Flight 14 as its first orbit attempt.
Starlink said Starship will launch 26 V3 satellites on Sept. 28.

items.means: European launch capacity can be sold as schedule insurance while Starship proves cadence, but that window closes quickly if Starship starts making orbit and reentry routine.

items.headline: Blue Origin asked the FAA to limit Starship operations at LC-39A.
items.current: Starship shifts into paid orbital missions
paragraphs: Blue Origin formally objected to the FAA’s draft environmental work for Starship launches at LC-39A, proposing reduced rates, new infrastructure, and compensation for other firms’ losses. If this slows Florida approvals, Starship growth stays concentrated in Texas longer than SpaceX would like.

items.headline: Exolaunch booked a 2029 Starfall return mission on Starship.
items.current: Starship shifts into paid orbital missions
paragraphs: Exolaunch contracted a Starfall mission targeted for 2029, its first move beyond rideshare into return-to-Earth services. Space Cargo Unlimited separately targeted a dedicated Starfall mission in 2028, but both bookings still depend on Starship reaching operational commercial flights.

items.headline: Judge cleared SpaceX’s 715-acre Texas refuge land swap.
items.current: Judge approves SpaceX Texas land swap
paragraphs: A federal judge denied an injunction, allowing SpaceX to proceed with a swap that transfers about 715 acres of wildlife refuge land to SpaceX in exchange for about 683 acres it owns. In parallel, local reporting says SpaceX has annexed 7,000 acres at Starbase, which would directly ease layout and logistics constraints if it holds.

items.headline: ISRO’s PSLV is 630 days without a success after two failures.
items.current: ISRO PSLV return to flight slips
paragraphs: PSLV’s consecutive third-stage failures in May 2025 and January 2026 have stretched into a 630-day gap without a successful launch and pulled its historical success rate down to about 92%. This matters outside India because PSLV has been a trusted rideshare option for small satellites that cannot always wait for premium Western manifests.

The immediate market effect is risk reallocation: rideshare buyers will push harder for schedule protection, and alternatives that can offer a credible return-to-flight and cadence will get the first call. That dynamic still favors launchers with already-proven chains of production and range access, because the new demand is for reliability, not experimentation.

block.head: PSLV’s reliability shock shows up as time without a success
block.title: Gaps between successful PSLV launches (as stated)

items.means: Customers who used PSLV as a baseline rideshare option will now budget for a second booking, which makes any dependable European small-launch capacity more valuable in negotiations.
